primary_sources.title: Quantum singular value transformation and beyond: exponential improvements for quantum matrix arithmetics

corollary18.summary: A real degree-n polynomial with parity n mod 2 and absolute value at most one on [-1,1] has a singular-value-transformation implementation. The proof lifts the real polynomial to a Corollary-8 polynomial P and averages P and P*.

lemma23.summary: For a degree-n Corollary-8 polynomial and matrices A,A_tilde of norm at most one satisfying ||A-A_tilde|| + ||(A+A_tilde)/2||^2 <= 1, the singular-value-transform perturbation is at most n*sqrt(2/(1-||(A+A_tilde)/2||^2))*||A-A_tilde||.

lemma29.summary: Constructs an even bounded rectangle polynomial with degree O(log(1/epsilon_prime)/delta_prime).

theorem30.summary: Uniform singular value amplification with gamma>1, delta,epsilon in (0,1/2), singular values up to (1-delta)/gamma, and degree O((gamma/delta) log(gamma/epsilon)).

proof_parameter_map.polynomial_properties: odd, bounded by one on [-1,1], epsilon-multiplicative approximation to gamma*x on [-(1-delta)/gamma,(1-delta)/gamma]

contracts.numeric_degree_limitation: Theorem 30, Lemma 29 and Lemma 25 expose asymptotic degree scaling but the inspected primary source does not state a numerical universal hidden constant sufficient to convert the big-O expression into a certified concrete degree.

primary_sources.title: Exponential quantum advantage in processing massive classical data

lemma_D8.summary: The locally stated quantum eigenvalue transform lemma in source-v1 is restricted to even real polynomial P and even integer d with |P(x)|<=1 on [-1,1].

lemma_D23_D214_D215.summary: The proof first approximates A/s with projected-block error epsilon_1, then states QSVT applies the odd linear function f(x)=s*x on [-1/s,1/s], with displayed degree O(s log(1/epsilon_2)) and output error epsilon_2 + O(d epsilon_1).

D216_D217.summary: The random-oracle channel error is accumulated across O(d) sparse-oracle uses; epsilon_3 is chosen of order epsilon/d, giving a sample-complexity structure proportional to d/epsilon_3 and therefore d^2/epsilon up to the source's common factors and logarithms.

primary_sources.interface_observation: The source-local Lemma D.8 as printed does not directly cover the odd linear polynomial used in D.23. Gilyen et al. Corollary 18 provides an imported odd-real-polynomial route, so this is an interface obligation rather than a theorem refutation.

non_claims: not a proof or refutation of QOS Lemma D.23 as a whole
not a certified numerical QSVT degree
not a realized or measured circuit depth
not a full-unitary or diamond-norm repaired D.23 guarantee
